content:
How much do we benefit from keeping the maximal universe diversity? Do we have an induction thing on the universe parameter similar to the changing \kappa argument on-paper (I know it's a wild idea)? When I experimented Hecke functors I found that the diversity quickly collapses to a singleton for the sake of brevity, but I am not sure if this is the correct way to do so.

Setup: Rep.{w u v} k G where
w for the underlying module V
u for the coefficient ring k
v for the group G and hence also for H : Subgroup G

The interesting object is of the form

IndHG1H.\mathrm{Ind}_H^G\mathbb{1}_H.IndHG​1H​.

To allow this object living in the desired category, we force w = max {v u} because the induction uses both k (as the underlying module of trivial representaiton) and H. Later we also want to use the closed monoidal instance for the dual and tensor product where it requires w = u(in Mathlib) so we have to verify u = w = max {v u}. It seems reasonable to just set u = v = w here, isn' it?
it's not possible to do "induction" on the universe
one place where having ungeneral universes is hurting is #mathlib4 > Universes restriction in Rep @ 💬

Aaron Liu said:

it's not possible to do "induction" on the universe

If it is not possible, then how do we formalize statements involving "enlarging Grothendieck universe"?
what's the statement?

e.g. Remark 1.4 https://www.math.uni-bonn.de/people/scholze/Condensed.pdf. I think there should be similar thing in the theory of fpqc sheaves (let me check)
Edit: the flat sheafification example is mentioned in mathlib4 > Universes restriction in Rep @ 💬

it doesn't look like there's any induction here

Remark 1.4. If κ′>κ\kappa' > \kappaκ′>κ are uncountable strong limit cardinals, there is an obvious forgetful functor from κ′\kappa'κ′-condensed sets to κ\kappaκ-condensed sets. This functor admits a natural left adjoint, which is a functor from κ\kappaκ-condensed sets to κ′\kappa'κ′-condensed sets. This functor is fully faithful and commutes with all colimits and many limits (in particular, all finite limits), as we will prove in Proposition 2.9 below. We will then define the category of condensed sets as the (large) colimit of the category of κ\kappaκ-condensed sets along the filtered poset of all uncountable strong limit cardinals κ\kappaκ.
You can very well go from Type u to Type (u + 1) if you need to enlarge the universe. For example the sheaf associated to a presheaf can have a universe bump (I think).

Anyway if universes are causing you too much headache my suggestion is just to ignore them and assume anything that makes your life easier. One can always try to fix those later, but note for example that Hilbert 90 currently only holds in Type.

Riccardo Brasca said:

Anyway if universes are causing you too much headache my suggestion is just to ignore them and assume anything that makes your life easier. One can always try to fix those later, but note for example that Hilbert 90 currently only holds in Type.

I wouldn't be surprise that big theorems will temporarily land in Type for technical reason. But all the above discussion didn't answer my original question (Aaron suggested to look at your post while Hilbert 90 currently only holds in Type still, so it seems that there is no enough benefit to make Hilbert 90 hold in Type* within the past six months).
in CGT we haven't gotten to the point where we have to use hilbert 90 yet, but we surely will eventually

Aaron Liu said:

it doesn't look like there's any induction here

A strong limit cardinal is not a Grothendieck universe, and you can do induction on strong limit cardinals in Lean no problem (and as Aaron points out, there doesn't seem to be any induction there).

@Jiaxi Mo Just because universes look like they are indexed by natural numbers, beware that the assumptions on what rules those need to follow is very much not an axiomatic arithmetic that has induction. Something like: there is a minimum element, succ u and max{u,v} and that's about it? I asked this once and got a nice answer, but it's floating around on the internet somewhere. And these indexes are meta-theory, right? So they better be not something like a model of PA....

Jiaxi Mo said:

It seems reasonable to just set u = v = w here, isn' it?

I think the policy is when you could make the universes polymorphic without too much trouble then you should almost always do so since this would benefit other people.

It seems that people are much more interested in the second nonsense question than the first direct question :sweat_smile: But I asked the second one exactly because I want to understand the first.

I think here seting u = v = w is similar to the Mathlib's instance : Monoidal Rep.{u} k G: we want to use Rep.of trivial k G k as unit so we set w = u. Do you have a plan to make this u more flexible?
you could use Shrink k instead

Another example I can tell now is the use of indResHomEquiv. I used the direction (A ⟶ res φ B) to (ind φ A ⟶ B) extensively to construct elements in Hecke modules. However I worked with Type* so the original categorical form is not ideal for direct application and what I did was isolating the code in indResHomEquiv.invFun to make it a Type* version def. I am not sure if this is plausible

For an example of experimentally varying this universe structure, you might have a look at An Order-Theoretic Analysis of Universe Polymorphism.
